reconcile.note: Clarke reads two entries of Satan into Judas, an earlier one before the meal and a second entry at the supper that confirmed his betrayal.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg lists it as a plain timing clash: Luke puts Satan's entry before the Last Supper, John only after.

quotes.text: When did Satan enter into Judas? Luke: Before the Last Supper ( xxii, 3–7 ). John: After the Last Supper ( xiii, 1–27 ).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on Luke 22:3 and John 13:27.

sides.snippet: Satan entered into Judas, who was surnamed Iscariot, who was numbered with the twelve.
sides.verseText: Satan entered into Judas, who was surnamed Iscariot, who was numbered with the twelve.

sides.snippet: After the piece of bread, then Satan entered into him.
sides.verseText: After the piece of bread, then Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to him, \"What you do, do quickly.\"
